title: Saffire-III, as recorded aboard the Cygnus cargo vehicle

zero.what: the first reading of the igniter current of sample S1 above half its maximum

window.rule: from 450 s before that ignition, or from the first live reading of the experiment if that is later, to the end of the file

units: NASA's file names its columns and gives no units. Readings are shown as recorded.

rules: An igniter or the smoke wire is on while its current is above half the largest current in its column.
The experiment's columns carry a reading in the rows where radiometer 1 differs from the value it holds in the first row, when the experiment was unpowered.
A radiometer's baseline is its median before the first smoke wire. It has risen, or is back, where it crosses 10% of the way from baseline to peak.
A vehicle channel carries a reading in the rows where it is not 0.
The detector's quiet level is its highest reading before the first smoke wire. Time above a level counts each reading until the next one.
The level used to compare the smoke wire with the fire is half the smoke wire's peak.

findings.detail: 1 row has a vehicle timestamp before 2001 (-62135597038000 ms); it is set aside.

The file interleaves the experiment's readings (about one a second) with the vehicle's. Each vehicle reading is written twice; a new detector value arrives about every 10.0 s, and between readings the column holds 0.
The columns of the other detector string (P@CDH_F1PCM_SMK_DET_SCAT_SENS_P, P@CDH_F1PCM_SMK_DET_OBS_SENS_P) hold 1 and 0 distinct non-zero values in the whole file.
The file gives no units, and the readme of the record does not describe these columns.

limits: One flight, one sample material, one flow speed. The flame burned in a duct whose exhaust entered the cabin.
The alarm level of the vehicle's detector is not in the file, so no alarm time is stated.
Smoke from the smoke wire and from the opposed-flow test was still in the cabin when the concurrent-flow sample was lit.
